audience.text: C++ developers building desktop, server, or embedded applications that require PDF document processing without external runtime dependencies.

capabilities.text: Open existing PDFs, including password-protected ones, and save changes with incremental metadata updates or full round-trips.
capabilities.title: Open and modify PDFs

capabilities.text: Extract full text using TextAbsorber and read/write document metadata via DocumentInfo and Metadata.
capabilities.title: Extract text and metadata

capabilities.text: Render pages to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or multi-page TIFF using PngDevice, JpegDevice, BmpDevice, and TiffDevice.
capabilities.title: Render pages to images

capabilities.text: Apply encryption with AES-256, AES-128, RC4-128, or RC4-40 using Document::Encrypt and Permissions flags.
capabilities.title: Encrypt and secure documents

capabilities.text: Build documents with positioned text, tables, vector shapes, watermarks, annotations, and AcroForm fields.
capabilities.title: Create content from scratch

capabilities.text: Add annotations (Highlight, Text, Link, etc.) and interactive AcroForm fields (TextBoxField, CheckboxField, etc.).
capabilities.title: Support for annotations and forms

capabilities.text: Use Facades classes like PdfConverter, PdfExtractor, PdfFileSignature, PdfFileEditor, and PdfFileStamp for common tasks.
capabilities.title: Facades API for legacy workflows

limitations.text: Standard-14 font fallback covers 12 of 14 fonts; Symbol and ZapfDingbats have no bundled fallback.
XmpValue type-checking helpers (IsDateTime, IsField, etc.) are stubs that always return false.
Setting metadata on a from-scratch document and saving throws because there is no /Info object to patch.
Permissions set via encryption are enforced by the consuming PDF viewer, not by this library.

problems_solved.text: Enables reading, writing, and modifying PDF documents in C++ without relying on commercial or third-party PDF libraries.
Provides text extraction, page rendering, and document encryption using only the C++ standard library.
Supports building PDFs from scratch with text, tables, graphics, annotations, and forms using a consistent API.

product_summary.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++ is a free, open-source C++20 library for creating, editing, and processing PDF documents with no runtime dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported AcroForm field types beyond those explicitly listed in examples is unclear.
Whether all Facades classes support all features of the commercial edition is not fully specified.
The behavior of TiffDevice with custom IIndexBitmapConverter is not detailed beyond signature.
The scope of 'byte-verbatim round-trips' for encrypted or signed documents is not clarified.
The exact set of supported PDF/A or PDF/UA features is not stated.
The handling of right-to-left or complex script text is not described.
Whether embedded font subsets beyond Standard-14 are supported is not stated.
The behavior of Document::Encrypt when called on an already encrypted document is not specified.

workflows.name: Open and inspect a PDF
workflows.text: Load a PDF file, count pages, read metadata, and check encryption status using Document, PageCollection, and DocumentInfo.

workflows.name: Extract text and render pages
workflows.text: Use TextAbsorber to extract text and PngDevice or TiffDevice to render pages to raster images.

workflows.name: Encrypt or sign a document
workflows.text: Apply encryption with Document::Encrypt using AES-256 or sign with Facades::PdfFileSignature.

workflows.name: Build a document from scratch
workflows.text: Create a new Document, add content via Paragraphs, Tables, Drawing::Graph, and annotations, then save.
